from __future__ import annotations

@app.get("/items/")
async def read_items(q: Annotated[str, Query(min_length = 3)] = ...):

comments.body:
on MacBook Pro M2 Max
PyCharm 2024.2.3 (Professional Edition)

Yeah, it seems that's wrong.

That also doesn't seem to be type hint compliant.

I think the wanted would have been:
```py
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import FastAPI, Query

app = FastAPI()


@app.get("/items/")
async def read_items(q: Annotated[str, Query(default=..., min_length=3)]):
    results = {"items": [{"item_id": "Foo"}, {"item_id": "Bar"}]}
    if q:
        results.update({"q": q})
    return results
```

I think that part of the docs is automatically generated from a script.
Please don't close it. This is a documentation issue. 😅

hi,Marcelo, I would like to confirm one more question about best practices:

Is it a recommended practice to make a parameter required by setting Query(default=...)? I noticed that using this method triggers another warning:
`PydanticJsonSchemaWarning: Default value Ellipsis is not JSON serializable; excluding default from JSON schema [non-serializable-default].`

So, I understand that the best practice to make a parameter required is to simply not assign a default value to it, for example:
```
@app.get("/validation")
async def async_root(str_param: Annotated[str, Query(min_length=3,
                                                     max_length=20,
                                                     pattern='^[a-zA-Z0-9]+$',
                                                     description='This is a string parameter')])
```

> So, I understand that the best practice to make a parameter required is to simply not assign a default value to it, for example:

Oh yeah, you are right. You don't need the `...` in that case.

I couldn't reproduce the `PydanticJsonSchemaWarning`. Can you provide a full MRE?

Okay, here it is. 
Let's try the following code:
```
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Annotated

import fastapi
import uvicorn
from fastapi import FastAPI, Query

app = FastAPI()
print(fastapi.__version__)


@app.get("/prepare")
async def prepare(str_param: Annotated[str, Query()] = ...):
    return {'str_param': str_param}


@app.get("/test")
async def full_mre(str_param: Annotated[str, Query(default = ...)]):
    return {'str_param': str_param}


if __name__ == '__main__':
    uvicorn.run(app, host = '127.0.0.1', port = 18081)
```
After running this code as a server, visit http://127.0.0.1:18081/docs#/default/prepare_prepare_get or http://127.0.0.1:18081/docs#/default/full_mre_test_get in your browser.
You will see that the warning appears only once when you first refresh the docs:
![QQ_1727606309174](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/83a24ad3-c5fe-4043-a2de-818a2cd8e230)

To be honest, reproducing this warning message is indeed a bit complex, 
I tried several combinations before I was able to reproduce it, and it doesn't appear consistently.
 it only triggers when the documentation is refreshed for the first time.

This is the part that reproduces the warning:

```py
from typing import Annotated

import uvicorn
from fastapi import FastAPI, Query

app = FastAPI()


@app.get("/prepare")
async def prepare(str_param: Annotated[str, Query()] = ...):
    return {"str_param": str_param}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run(app, host="127.0.0.1", port=18081)
```

It makes sense, but we already said that this is not needed. You can just do:
```py
@app.get("/prepare")
async def prepare(str_param: Annotated[str, Query()]):
    return {"str_param": str_param}
```

You only see the issue on the first time you call `/docs` because that's when the OpenAPI is generated. After that, the OpenAPI object is cached.
Note that in Pydantic, we recently moved away from using the ellipsis, and we now recommend against using it: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/10661.

> Note that in Pydantic, we recently moved away from using the ellipsis, and we now recommend against using it: [pydantic/pydantic#10661](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/10661).

The problem here is what is in the documentation.

I started looking into it, by discouraging using the ellipsis in docs. But I realized FastAPI still supports Pydantic V1, where `f: Optional[<type>]` is different from `f: Optional[<type>] = ...` (because in V1 `Optional[...]` added a default value of `None`, so the ellipsis was a way to still make it required). Maybe it's best to wait for FastAPI to drop support for V1 so that the documentation can easily be updated.
- Given https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/issues/10360, I don't think it makes sense for FastAPI to support V1 anymore.

Thanks for the discussion everyone! This was handled here: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/13377

Ellipsis is discouraged and has been for quite a while. Those particular docs examples were not tested, and indeed they were failing. I just updated those docs to use the newest version of the language syntax and the recommended patterns.

I'll now close this issue, thanks all! ☕

title: Required with Ellipsis may not work
